settings:
# Exploratory follow-up of 12.11.2026 (course folder pro/followup-2026-11-12/plan.md), chosen after the main
# results and two reviews. Not in the plan; decides no hypothesis. Bars and predictions below were
# written before the run. "Reduction" is the relative error reduction of the main report.
#
# N1, size study inside the benchmark. The 10 datasets with at least 4,700 outer-training rows, seed 0. Each
# outer-training set is cut to 250, 1,000 and 4,000 rows (nested, class proportions kept); the test rows
# stay the same; preprocessing is refitted on the smaller set, so d and K can change and are recorded.
# Full size is content.toml. 3 x 5 x 10 x 5 = 750 tasks.
#
# Bars (per dataset, comparing 250 rows with full size; "most" = at least 8 of 10):
# - S1 the noise penalty shrinks with rows: the reduction of target_noise_xx against base is higher at full
#   size than at 250 rows on most datasets. Read at layer 1 and at the chosen layer. Prediction: no at
#   layer 1, yes at the chosen layer (the saved runs show the trend only there).
# - S2 the net effect grows with rows: the same for residual_xx against base. Prediction: open.
# - S3 redundancy: the reduction of target_xx against target_noise_xx falls with rows on most datasets.
#   Prediction: open.
# S1 at layer 1 supports "extra columns overfit small data"; S1 only at the chosen layer says depth
# repairs the damage; S3 says larger data makes the products redundant.
datasets = ["parkinsons", "air_quality", "ccpp", "phishing", "bike_sharing", "bank_marketing", "adult",
            "credit_default", "california", "superconductivity"]
seeds = [0]
outer_folds = 5

[[check]]
name = "n250"
methods = ["base", "random_xx", "target_xx", "residual_xx", "target_noise_xx"]
cascade = { train_rows = 250 }

[[check]]
name = "n1000"
methods = ["base", "random_xx", "target_xx", "residual_xx", "target_noise_xx"]
cascade = { train_rows = 1000 }

[[check]]
name = "n4000"
methods = ["base", "random_xx", "target_xx", "residual_xx", "target_noise_xx"]
cascade = { train_rows = 4000 }
